title: Using the Amazon Product Advertising API with 4D
featured_technology: Amazon Product Advertising API (SOAP and REST)
HMAC-SHA256 request signing via a custom 4D OpenSSL Plugin
DOM Parse XML source for REST calls
4D Internet Commands-based custom SOAP call (bypassing CALL WEB SERVICE)
4D AWS Library component with XSLT-based request generation (APPLY XSLT TRANSFORMATION)

historical_commentary.text: This note is a genuinely advanced piece of web-services engineering for its time, working around three real limitations of 4D v11 SQL's built-in SOAP client (no complex response parsing, no multi-element SOAP headers, and no native HMAC-SHA256) by writing a custom OpenSSL-calling plugin and hand-built SOAP/REST request logic. However, the specific target — Amazon's 2009-era Product Advertising API (then requiring only HMAC-SHA256 and an AWS access key) — is obsolete: Amazon has since retired that SOAP interface, deprecated multiple REST API versions, and now requires AWS Signature Version 4 plus an active, sales-qualified Associates account under the current Product Advertising API 5.0, so none of this Tech Note's request-signing or endpoint code will work against Amazon's API as it exists today. The general SOAP/REST/HMAC workaround techniques remain instructive, but the concrete Amazon integration is non-functional as written.
related_updates: Amazon Product Advertising API 5.0 (current) requires AWS Signature Version 4 and an active, sales-qualifying Associates account — incompatible with this note's HMAC-SHA256-only signing scheme
4D now has native HTTP/REST request commands and built-in cryptographic hashing (SHA-family) commands, removing the need for a custom OpenSSL-calling plugin
Modern 4D REST + ORDA and native JSON support make ad-hoc XSLT-based request generation largely unnecessary for calling REST APIs
